title: Slew-Rate Limiter Model
constraints: `SR` is the slew rate in V/s and `TS` the clock period in s. The maximum step per edge is `SR · TS`.
On each rising edge, `vout` moves toward `vin` by at most `SR · TS`. If `vin` is closer than that, `vout = vin` exactly.
The judge uses `SR = 2.0e7` (0.2 V per 10 ns step). `vout` starts at 0.0. Tolerance 1e-9 V.
hints: Compute `d = vin - vout` and clamp it to [−SR·TS, +SR·TS].
Then `vout += clamped_d`, which automatically lands exactly on `vin` when |d| is small.
The step size is a constant: declare it as a `localparam real` / `constant`.
